findings.title: Nil request dereference in ContextualLoggerMiddleware panics when req is nil
findings.body: `ContextualLoggerMiddleware.QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth`, and `CollectMetrics` (lines 40, 45, 50, 55) unconditionally dereference `req.PluginContext` before passing the request down the middleware chain. Previously, `InstrumentationMiddleware` only called `instrumentContext` after `m.pluginTarget` succeeded, and `LoggerMiddleware` explicitly guards against `req == nil` (e.g. `if req == nil { return m.next.QueryData(ctx, req) }` in `logger_middleware.go`). Because `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is registered ahead of `LoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares`, any call with a `nil` request (such as those tested in `logger_middleware_test.go` or `tracing_middleware_test.go`) will panic with a nil pointer dereference when `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` is in the chain.

findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a new instance, discarding recorded logs on the receiver
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of `f`. In `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest`, logging was changed from `m.logger.Info(...)` to `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`. Any test that passes a `*log.TestLogger` into `NewLoggerMiddleware` (such as `logger_middleware_test.go`) and inspects `testLogger.InfoLogs` will now see zero recorded calls because the log entry is written to the freshly allocated `TestLogger` returned by `FromContext` and immediately discarded.
